questions.question: Which company's logo is this?
questions.explanation: The designer added the bite so that, at a small size, people would see an apple and not a cherry.

media.alt: A black piece of fruit with a bite taken out

questions.question: Which sports brand's logo is this?
questions.explanation: The swoosh was drawn in 1971 by a student, Carolyn Davidson, who was paid just 35 dollars for it.

media.alt: A black curved tick shape

questions.question: Which restaurant chain's logo is this?
questions.explanation: The golden arches copy the real yellow arches that stood on the sides of the early restaurants in the 1950s.

media.alt: Two yellow arches side by side

questions.question: Which app's icon is this?
questions.explanation: The red box comes from the first logo, where it held the word 'Tube', an old nickname for a television.

media.alt: A white triangle on a red rounded rectangle

questions.question: Which games brand's logo is this?
questions.explanation: The logo is a P standing upright on an S lying flat, the first letters of the brand's name.

media.alt: A black symbol made of two chunky shapes

questions.question: Which game's app icon is this?
questions.explanation: The tilted square started life as the letter O in the game's name, drawn as a square tipped on its side.

media.alt: A tilted white square on a blue background

questions.question: Which football club's crest is this?
questions.explanation: The cockerel wears fighting spurs, a nod to Harry Hotspur, the medieval knight the club is named after.

media.alt: A football crest with a cockerel standing on a ball

questions.question: Which football club's crest is this?
questions.explanation: Wolves is short for Wolverhampton, and a wolf's head has been the club badge on its gold shirts since 1979.

media.alt: A black animal's head on an orange-gold badge

questions.question: Which coffee shop chain's logo is this?
questions.explanation: The lady in green is a siren, a mermaid with two tails from old sea stories, because the first shop was in the port city of Seattle.

media.alt: A green circle with a crowned woman with long wavy hair

questions.question: Which games console's icon is this?
questions.explanation: The icon shows the console's two Joy-Con controllers, one on each side, ready to click into place.

media.alt: A red icon of two rounded halves, each with a circle

questions.question: Which learning app's mascot is this?
questions.explanation: The green owl is called Duo, and he is famous online for nagging people who forget their daily lesson.

media.alt: A bright green cartoon owl

questions.question: Which car maker's badge is this?
questions.explanation: The three points of the star stand for land, sea and air, because the company built engines for all three.

media.alt: A three-pointed star inside a circle

questions.question: Which car maker's badge is this?
questions.explanation: Each ring stands for one of four car companies that joined together in 1932: Audi, DKW, Horch and Wanderer.

media.alt: Four black rings linked in a row

questions.question: Which phone software uses this robot as its logo?
questions.explanation: Designer Irina Blok drew the green robot in 2007, and said she got the idea from the little people on toilet door signs.

media.alt: A green robot with two antennae

questions.question: Which music app's logo is this?
questions.explanation: The app began in Sweden in 2006, and its three curved lines look like sound waves coming out of a speaker.

media.alt: Three curved black lines on a green circle

questions.question: Which payment card's logo is this?
questions.explanation: In 2019 the company dropped its name from the logo, trusting the two overlapping circles to speak for themselves.

media.alt: A red circle and an orange circle overlapping

questions.question: Which social network used this bird as its logo until 2023?
questions.explanation: The bird was nicknamed Larry, after the Boston Celtics basketball star Larry Bird, before it was replaced by an X.

media.alt: A blue bird in flight

questions.question: Which football club's crest is this?
questions.explanation: The crown was added in 1920, when King Alfonso XIII gave the club the title 'Real', meaning royal.

media.alt: A gold-edged football crest with a crown on top

questions.question: Which web browser's logo is this?
questions.explanation: Firefox is another name for the red panda, yet the animal curled round the logo is drawn as a fox.

media.alt: An orange animal curled round a purple ball

questions.question: Which games console brand's logo is this?
questions.explanation: The name comes from the console's working title, the DirectX Box, after Microsoft's DirectX graphics software.

media.alt: A white X across a green sphere

questions.question: Which car maker's badge is this?
questions.explanation: The name means 'three diamonds', and the badge blends the family crest of founder Yataro Iwasaki with that of the Tosa clan.

media.alt: Three red diamonds meeting in the middle

questions.question: Which car maker's badge is this?
questions.explanation: Unveiled in 1989, its two inner ovals stand for the hearts of the customer and the company, held inside a third.

media.alt: Three red ovals, two of them crossing inside the third

questions.question: Which football club's crest is this?
questions.explanation: In 2017 the club swapped its traditional oval crest for this simple black-and-white J, to plenty of grumbling from fans.

media.alt: A tall black letter made of two stripes

questions.question: Which computer operating system has this penguin as its mascot?
questions.explanation: Linus Torvalds wanted a penguin, saying he had once been nipped by one at a zoo in Australia; it is called Tux.

media.alt: A cartoon penguin sitting down

questions.question: Which wireless technology uses this symbol?
questions.explanation: It joins the runes for H and B, the initials of Harald Bluetooth, a Viking king of Denmark.

media.alt: A white angular symbol on a blue rounded shape

questions.question: Which football club's crest is this?
questions.explanation: The club are the Rams, a nod to the local regiment's ram mascot and the old folk song 'The Derby Ram'.

media.alt: A black outline of a ram with curled horns

questions.question: Which video game company's logo is this?
questions.explanation: Fans call it the 'Fuji' because it looks like Japan's famous mountain, though its designer meant it as a letter A.

media.alt: Three black stripes, the outer two curving outwards at the bottom

questions.question: Which American TV network's logo is this?
questions.explanation: The peacock first appeared in 1956 to show off the network's new colour broadcasts.

media.alt: Six colourful feathers fanned out

questions.question: Which car maker's badge is this?
questions.explanation: The slanted H is meant to show two people shaking hands: the company and its customer.

media.alt: A slanted letter inside a blue oval

questions.question: Which airline's logo is this?
questions.explanation: The flying crane was drawn in 1918 by designer Otto Firle, years before the airline itself was founded in 1926.

media.alt: A flying bird inside a circle
